# Hosts that answer automated requests with bot protection instead of the real
# status code (HTTP 403/429/999, login walls, or a TLS reset). Links on these
# hosts are reported as "allowlisted" and never fail the build.
#
# Format:  <host>[/<path prefix>]   # reason
# A bare host also covers its subdomains (linkedin.com covers www.linkedin.com).
# Keep this list short: every entry is a link nobody is checking any more.
# Review it whenever you bump the checker version.

linkedin.com          # HTTP 999 / login wall for non-browser clients
g2.com                # Cloudflare challenge on automated requests
crunchbase.com        # Cloudflare challenge on automated requests
producthunt.com       # Cloudflare challenge on automated requests
reddit.com            # HTTP 403/429 for datacenter IP ranges
x.com                 # login wall, HTTP 200 with an empty shell
twitter.com           # login wall, HTTP 200 with an empty shell
instagram.com         # login wall
facebook.com          # login wall
tiktok.com            # Cloudflare challenge
quora.com             # Cloudflare challenge
medium.com            # Cloudflare challenge
glassdoor.com         # HTTP 403 for datacenter IP ranges
wellfound.com         # Cloudflare challenge
youtube.com           # intermittent HTTP 429 from shared CI runners
